title: Rosalind and the Echo
premise: Mirabel Ravensworth keeps the Halcyon Beacon running alone, guarding a hold full of illegal consciousness backups she was ordered to destroy and never did. When the deep-space vessel Vantablack returns with its crew aged backward into childhood, Mirabel discovers the beacon is a resurrection engine: it has been slowly rebuilding one of those backups, a woman named Rosalind, from stolen signal echoes. As two rival fleets converge to claim or destroy the beacon, Mirabel must sustain the fiction that Earth's final transmission still authorizes her command — a lie holding the peace together — while deciding whether Rosalind is a person, a weapon, or herself. In the end, Mirabel broadcasts the truth of every backup in the hold, shattering both fleets' claims; Rosalind chooses erasure over becoming anyone's prize, and Mirabel inherits the beacon as a sanctuary rather than a secret.
about_author: Xanthe Thornbury is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who left observatory work to write about machines that outlive their makers. They live off-grid on a decommissioned listening station, where they repair antique transmitters and insist the static sometimes answers.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She performs her lonely maintenance rounds aboard the beacon station, lying in her logs about crew numbers and quietly feeding power to the sealed backup hold. Establishes her guilt, routine, and the strange harmonic the beacon emits at night. Emotional beat: complicity disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Signal from a Dead Year
chapters.summary: Mirabel intercepts a transmission dated eleven years in the future — Earth's last broadcast, looping. She recognizes her own voice buried in its metadata. Flashback reveals she signed the order to purge the backups and never executed it. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: Vantablack
chapters.summary: A derelict ship drifts into range: the Vantablack, missing for decades, its crew now children wearing adult memories' clothes. Mirabel docks against protocol. The eldest 'child,' a girl called Sef, speaks in navigational jargon and calls Mirabel by name. POV alternates briefly with Sef. Emotional beat: uncanny grief.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Investigating the Vantablack's logs, Mirabel learns its crew attempted time-dilated return and were de-aged by exposure to the beacon's own echo field. The beacon isn't just transmitting — it's remembering people backward. She checks the hold: one backup pod has begun cycling. Emotional beat: horror at her own complicity.

chapters.title: Rosalind
chapters.summary: The pod opens. A woman steps out calling herself Rosalind, with no past except fragments that mirror Mirabel's own memories — including the purge order. Rosalind is calm, curious, and terrifyingly fluent in Mirabel's private history. Emotional beat: recognition without explanation.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on One Horizon
chapters.summary: Fleet contacts appear: the Concordat, claiming salvage rights, and the Meridian Compact, claiming the beacon as stolen sovereign property. Both demand Mirabel authenticate command authority. She invokes Earth's last transmission loop — technically expired, practically unverifiable. Emotional beat: the lie begins.

chapters.title: The Architecture of a Lie
chapters.summary: Mirabel forges authentication handshakes to keep both fleets at standoff distance, buying days. Rosalind watches her work and asks why Mirabel protects the backups she once condemned. Their argument becomes the book's moral spine. Emotional beat: intimacy built on interrogation.

chapters.title: Sef's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The de-aged crew children are aging forward again, but unevenly — some faster than others, as if the beacon rations them. Sef deduces the beacon is using them as calibration. She confronts Mirabel, forcing her to admit she doesn't control the machine. Emotional beat: betrayed trust.

chapters.title: Concordat Boarding Party
chapters.summary: A Concordat officer, Ives Calloway, boards under inspection pretense and finds the empty pod. He suspects Rosalind exists and offers Mirabel extraction in exchange for the backup manifest. She refuses; he leaves a tracker. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Echoes of the Purge Order
chapters.summary: Rosalind recovers more of her origin: she is compiled from the beacon's echo of Mirabel's own transmissions during the purge year — part witness, part accusation. Mirabel must reckon that she may have built her own judge. Emotional beat: shame metabolizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends
chapters.summary: Earth's last transmission finally terminates. Within hours, both fleets detect the gap and begin moving on the beacon. Mirabel fabricates an extension so seamless it fools even her own systems — and realizes the lie now runs itself. Emotional beat: vertigo of mastery.

chapters.title: Children of the Return
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. The Vantablack children, half-restored, vote on whether to side with Mirabel or bargain with the fleets for full restoration. Sef argues for Mirabel; the majority wavers toward the fleets' promises. Emotional beat: hope auctioned.

chapters.title: Calloway's Truth
chapters.summary: Calloway returns, confessing the Concordat intends to strip the beacon for its echo technology and let the children lapse. He offers this as leverage, wanting asylum for himself. Mirabel must decide whether a traitor's truth can be trusted. Emotional beat: alliance across bad faith.

chapters.title: What Power Wants
chapters.summary: Meridian Compact envoy Adeyemi boards and, unlike Calloway, tells the truth openly: the Compact wants Rosalind as proof-of-concept for immortality by echo, and will take the station by force if refused. She gives Mirabel six hours. Emotional beat: clarity before the storm.

chapters.title: Six Hours
chapters.summary: Mirabel, Rosalind, Sef, and Calloway plan. Options narrow to surrendering Rosalind, destroying the beacon, or broadcasting everything. Rosalind proposes a fourth path only she can attempt: entering the echo core to speak to whatever the beacon has become. Emotional beat: resolve crystallizing.

chapters.title: Into the Core
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV inside the echo field: a cathedral of stored voices, including every backup Mirabel saved and the original Rosalind whose death seeded it all. She learns the beacon has been waiting for someone to choose on behalf of the dead. Emotional beat: awe and sorrow entwined.

chapters.title: The Fleets Arrive
chapters.summary: Both fleets reach weapons range as the fabricated authorization collapses publicly. Mirabel, exposed as a fraud, loses command legitimacy — and with it, the fragile peace. Boarders breach the station. Emotional beat: the cost of the lie coming due.

chapters.title: Every Voice at Once
chapters.summary: Climax. Rosalind triggers a station-wide broadcast: every backup's voice, every de-aged crew member's testimony, the purge order in Mirabel's own words. Both fleets' crews hear their own dead speaking. Weapons hold. Mutiny spreads through both formations. Emotional beat: justice outside any law.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Choice
chapters.summary: Offered personhood by one fleet and weaponization by the other, Rosalind refuses both. She disperses herself back into the echo field, freeing the stored voices to fade honestly rather than be owned. Mirabel begs her to stay; Rosalind says being remembered is not the same as being kept. Emotional beat: devastating grace.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: The fleets withdraw, their crews refusing orders to fire on a station full of witnesses. Sef and the restored Vantablack crew elect to remain. Calloway takes the full story to open channels. Mirabel faces formal inquiry but finds the charges dissolving in public sentiment. Emotional beat: exhausted relief.

chapters.title: The Inquiry of Mirabel Ravensworth
chapters.summary: Mirabel testifies to everything — the forged authorizations, the saved backups, the lie that held two fleets apart. Judgment is suspended pending a new interfleet accord she never asked to inspire. She is returned to the beacon, neither pardoned nor punished. Emotional beat: accountability without absolution.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Echo
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Mirabel's POV. She reopens the beacon as a sanctuary where the fading voices can be visited, not owned. On quiet nights the harmonic returns, and once — only once — it shapes itself into a word that might be her name. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
